title: Something is off
text: For several days, ordinary tasks have felt harder than they should. It could be nothing, or it could be the first clue that your body needs attention.

outcomes.text: The appointment catches a problem early enough to make a plan.

thread.title: The checkup I did not postpone
thread.memory: I listened when my body stopped feeling ordinary.

outcomes.text: The tests are reassuring. The relief is almost physical.

choices.label: Rest and watch it for a week

outcomes.text: Sleep, water and a slower schedule are enough. The strange fatigue lifts.
The feeling lingers. Waiting did not answer the question.
Adrenaline carries the week, but the crash arrives on the weekend.
For once, stubbornness gets lucky and the feeling passes.

title: The symptom returns
text: The problem you hoped would disappear has returned clearly enough that ignoring it now feels like a choice.

outcomes.text: A clinician takes the history seriously and gives you a treatment plan.

thread.title: The symptom that came back
thread.memory: A problem returned until I finally gave it proper attention.

outcomes.text: The answer is not immediate, but the next test is finally the right one.
A second set of eyes spots something the first visit missed.
The second opinion agrees with the first: monitor it, but do not panic.
The uncertainty becomes its own source of stress.
It settles again, but you know the question is still waiting.

title: Two doctors, two answers
text: A treatment plan does not sit right with you. Another clinic is willing to review the case, but it means another bill and another round of waiting.

outcomes.text: The second doctor changes the plan and explains why. You leave with more confidence than certainty.
They reach the same conclusion independently. That agreement is calming.

choices.label: Ask your current doctor more questions

outcomes.text: The extra conversation clears up what the rushed appointment did not.
The explanation still feels thin. You leave frustrated.
The treatment begins to help exactly as expected.
Side effects make the plan harder than the diagnosis did.

title: The cure has a cost
text: A new medication is helping one problem while creating another: dizziness, stomach trouble and a foggy afternoon.

outcomes.text: The dose is adjusted and the side effects ease within days.
You switch medications. The transition is annoying, but manageable.
Your body adapts after an unpleasant week.
The side effects get worse and start interfering with work and sleep.
The original symptoms return quickly.
You feel better at first, then worry about whether stopping suddenly was smart.

title: An old injury speaks up
text: A familiar ache returns after a long day. It is not dramatic, but your body remembers exactly where you were hurt.

outcomes.text: You scale back, do the exercises and wake up moving better.

thread.title: What my body remembers
thread.memory: An old ache taught me that recovery is maintenance, not a finish line.

outcomes.text: Rest helps, but the stiffness is stubborn enough to schedule a follow-up.
The ache fades once you warm up. You got away with it.
By evening, compensation has turned one sore spot into three.

choices.label: Use it as an excuse for a quiet day

outcomes.text: A quiet day becomes exactly what you needed.
You rest physically and spiral mentally about getting older.

title: A wave with no warning
text: Your heart races, your breathing goes shallow and the room suddenly feels too small. Nothing obvious is happening around you, but your body has sounded an alarm.

outcomes.text: The wave peaks and passes. You stay where you are and let your nervous system catch up.

thread.title: The first time I rode out the wave
thread.memory: I learned that a frightening body alarm could pass without controlling the whole day.

outcomes.text: It takes longer than you hoped, but you get through it without running.
A familiar voice helps the room become ordinary again.
They mean well but do not understand. You still feel less alone afterward.
You finish what you were doing, then feel wrung out for the rest of the day.
The fear of another episode becomes louder than the episode itself.

title: The hard conversation
text: After another difficult spell, someone close to you gently asks whether you have considered getting support instead of carrying it alone.

outcomes.text: The first session is mostly history and awkward honesty, but it feels like a beginning.

thread.title: I asked for support
thread.memory: I stopped treating support as something I had to earn by getting worse first.

outcomes.text: The first therapist is not a good fit. You decide that one mismatch is not the same as treatment failing.

choices.label: Talk to your regular doctor first

outcomes.text: The doctor screens carefully and helps you understand the options.
You leave with a referral and a shorter list of unknowns.
They accept the answer and remind you the offer stands.
You get defensive, then regret the argument later.

title: Everything feels urgent
text: Emails, errands and obligations have blurred together. You are still functioning, but every small request now feels like someone adding a brick to your backpack.

outcomes.text: One unscheduled day does not solve your life, but your shoulders finally drop.
You spend half the day feeling guilty, then realize the world kept turning.
Your boss redistributes a project before it becomes a crisis.
The answer is polite and useless. At least you now know where you stand.

choices.label: Work even harder to get ahead

outcomes.text: You clear the backlog and feel unstoppable for approximately six hours.
You make an exhausted mistake that creates even more work.

title: A date on the calendar
text: You realize why today felt strange before breakfast: it is an anniversary connected to someone you lost.

outcomes.text: You make space for the memory without demanding a particular emotion from yourself.

thread.title: The date I still notice
thread.memory: Some anniversaries remained in my body even when I was not counting the years.

outcomes.text: The ritual is heavier than expected, but still worth doing.

choices.label: Spend time with family or friends

outcomes.text: Someone tells a story you had never heard. For a moment, the person feels present in the room.
The gathering is messy and emotional, which turns out to be honest rather than bad.

choices.label: Treat it like any other day

outcomes.text: Routine carries you through. The memory waits quietly in the background.
You snap at someone over something tiny and only later understand why.

title: Not medically necessary
text: A letter says the treatment your doctor recommended is not covered as submitted. The phrase “not medically necessary” appears three times.

outcomes.text: A corrected code and a stubborn phone call get the claim approved.
The appeal drags on, but you reduce the bill enough to matter.
It hurts the bank account, but treatment starts on time.
The bill is larger than expected and follows you for months.
The delay does not change the outcome, but the waiting is miserable.
The condition worsens enough that the later care is harder.

title: A quieter anniversary
text: You notice that a difficult chapter—an addiction, illness, injury or mental-health crisis—is no longer the first thing you think about every morning.

outcomes.text: You let yourself be proud without pretending recovery was linear.

thread.title: The year life became larger again
thread.memory: Recovery stopped being the whole story and became one chapter of it.

outcomes.text: Pride brings unexpected grief for the time the struggle took from you.

choices.label: Help someone earlier in the process

outcomes.text: Listening without lecturing helps both of you.
You realize their story is not yours and step back before becoming overinvolved.
Ordinary life is the celebration. You enjoy that thought.
You barely notice the date until bedtime, which might be its own kind of progress.

title: They noticed too
text: A relative tells you, carefully, that you have seemed exhausted and unlike yourself lately. Their concern lands somewhere between comforting and irritating.

choices.label: Tell them what has been going on

outcomes.text: Saying it plainly turns vague worry into something the two of you can actually discuss.
You get emotional halfway through the explanation. They stay anyway.

choices.label: Thank them, but keep details private

outcomes.text: They respect the boundary and still offer practical help.
They back off, though the concern does not quite leave their face.
They drop the subject. You immediately feel guilty for biting their head off.
The denial almost convinces you too, at least until the next bad day.

title: Water where water should not be
text: You step into the hallway and your sock finds a cold puddle. A pipe inside the wall has chosen today to become a fountain.

outcomes.text: The leak is stopped before it reaches the electrical work.

thread.title: The night the wall started leaking
thread.memory: Homeownership once meant standing in a hallway at midnight listening for water.

outcomes.text: The plumber fixes the pipe but finds older corrosion nearby.
You shut off the water and make a surprisingly competent temporary repair.
Your patch redirects the leak into a worse place. Professional help now costs more.

choices.label: Put a bucket under it for now

outcomes.text: The bucket works until morning. Sleep does not.
The ceiling below stains before you admit the bucket was not a plan.

title: What was behind the wall
text: The repaired section is opened again for finishing work, and the contractor finds something nobody expected.

choices.label: Fix everything while the wall is open

outcomes.text: It is expensive, but the hidden problem is gone instead of waiting for another year.
The contractor finds less damage than feared and the final bill is merciful.
The minimum repair holds. You make a note to budget for the rest.
The untouched section immediately becomes a new source of worry.
The second estimate is lower and better explained.
The second contractor agrees with the first. At least the bad news is consistent.

title: Bass through the wall
text: Your neighbor has discovered a speaker capable of shaking framed photographs. It is 1:14 in the morning.

outcomes.text: They look embarrassed, turn it down and later bring over an apology snack.

thread.title: The neighbor with the enormous speaker
thread.memory: One awkward midnight conversation became the beginning of knowing the people next door.

outcomes.text: They turn it down for exactly twenty minutes, then forget the conversation happened.
The music stops quickly. Eye contact on the driveway becomes complicated.
The complaint starts a petty little cold war over bins, parking and hedges.
Cheap foam saves the night and maybe the relationship.
You sleep badly and spend breakfast composing arguments you never deliver.

title: A peace offering
text: After months of ridiculous tension, the neighbor appears with coffee and an awkward apology about how far the feud went.

outcomes.text: You both laugh at the pettiness. The street feels lighter afterward.

thread.title: The feud that became a joke
thread.memory: A petty neighborhood war ended because someone finally knocked on a door with coffee.

outcomes.text: The truce is cautious, but genuine enough to stop the nonsense.
Civility returns without pretending you are suddenly friends.
They seem disappointed, but respect the boundary.
The coffee leaves with them. So does the easiest chance to end the feud.
You make your point and immediately wonder why winning feels this tiring.

title: The envelope with the tiny font
text: The neighborhood association has opinions about your front yard, mailbox and apparently the exact emotional tone of your fence.

outcomes.text: A small weekend project makes the letter disappear.
The repair costs more than it should, but the inspection passes.
You find the bylaw they misread and the notice is withdrawn.
The board has the rule on its side. You lose an evening and still have to fix it.
Nothing happens for months. You start to think the threat was mostly stationery.
A fine arrives with a second fine attached to it.

title: A smell after rain
text: One room develops a damp, earthy smell whenever it rains. Moving the furniture reveals a dark patch near the baseboard.

outcomes.text: The source is a small leak and the remediation is contained.
The inspector finds a larger moisture problem behind the wall.
You remove the visible patch and fix the loose seal causing it.
The spot returns twice as large after the next storm.

choices.label: Close the door and deal with it later

outcomes.text: The smell stays contained long enough to become easy to rationalize.
The dampness spreads and someone in the house develops a cough.

title: The damp came back
text: The moisture problem returns after another season. This time there is no pretending it was only a stain.

outcomes.text: Walls come down, fans run for days and the house finally smells normal again.
The work reveals one more repair, but solving it now prevents a much bigger bill.
Competition knocks hundreds off the price without cutting corners.
All three bids are awful in roughly the same way.
The buyer catches it during inspection and renegotiates hard.
You disclose the issue, price accordingly and walk away relieved.

title: The house finally feels inhabited
text: The boxes are mostly gone and the rooms are beginning to look like decisions instead of temporary storage.

outcomes.text: People spill into the kitchen, someone starts music and the place finally sounds lived in.

thread.title: The first crowded night here
thread.memory: The house became a home when people I cared about filled it with noise.

outcomes.text: The party is chaotic, one glass breaks and everyone stays later than planned.
A reading chair, a lamp and a few deliberate choices change the whole mood.
You overspend a little, but the room makes you smile every time you pass it.
The responsible choice is not glamorous, but the emergency fund feels good.
You save the cash and immediately get annoyed by the blank walls.

title: The storm tests the house
text: Wind drives rain sideways and the lights flicker hard enough to make everyone stop talking.

choices.label: Check the roof and windows safely

outcomes.text: A loose shutter and one small leak are the worst of it.
You catch a window seal failing before it floods the room.

choices.label: Stay inside and wait it out

outcomes.text: The house groans all night and holds.
A branch lands on the fence before dawn.

choices.label: Invite the neighbors over if their power is out

outcomes.text: Extension cords, candles and shared food turn a miserable night into a neighborhood story.

thread.title: The blackout night
thread.memory: A storm turned neighboring houses into one temporary household.

outcomes.text: More people show up than expected. It is crowded, loud and strangely comforting.

title: An unsolicited offer
text: A buyer sends a surprisingly serious offer for your house even though it is not listed.

outcomes.text: You realize the house means more to you than the number on the page.

thread.title: The offer I turned down
thread.memory: Someone tried to put a number on the house, and I learned what the place meant to me.

outcomes.text: You decline, then spend a week wondering whether you just walked away from perfect timing.
The buyer raises the offer enough to make the decision genuinely difficult.
They disappear the moment you counter. Apparently the “serious” offer had limits.

choices.label: Use it as a reason to evaluate the house

outcomes.text: An appraisal shows you have built more equity than you realized.
The appraisal is lower than the offer, which makes the mystery even stranger.

title: The casino knows your name
text: A glossy envelope offers a free suite, dinner and a private table if you return this weekend.

choices.label: Take the comp and set a hard budget

outcomes.text: You enjoy the room, eat the expensive dinner and leave the table before the night changes shape.

thread.title: The invitation with my name on it
thread.memory: Winning enough made the casino start treating me like a customer worth remembering.

outcomes.text: The budget survives, but only because you walk away during a hot streak.

choices.label: Take the comp and play like a VIP

outcomes.text: The table loves you tonight. The free room suddenly looks very cheap to the casino.
The hospitality was free because your losing streak was not.
The envelope hits the trash unopened. Your evening stays yours.
You keep thinking about the offer, but not going still saves money.

title: House money
text: After a strong run at the tables, your shopping list suddenly looks much less responsible and much more interesting.

outcomes.text: You spend part of the win on something you were going to buy anyway. Future you approves.
The “useful” purchase somehow comes with three accessories.

choices.label: Go on a ridiculous shopping spree

outcomes.text: For one afternoon, every price tag feels fictional.

thread.title: The win I turned into bags
thread.memory: Casino money became real the moment I carried it out of a shop.

outcomes.text: The bags are impressive. The bank balance the next morning is less so.
The win sits untouched long enough to feel like savings instead of luck.
You save it all and still spend the night mentally replaying the table.

title: Just get back to even
text: A bad session leaves you staring at the balance and doing the dangerous math: one more bet could erase the whole loss.

outcomes.text: You walk outside while still angry. Ten minutes later, leaving feels like the only win that mattered.

thread.title: The night I stopped chasing
thread.memory: I learned that a loss did not become a debt I owed the casino.

outcomes.text: You leave, but the unfinished feeling follows you home.
It wins, but not enough to make the night whole. You leave anyway.
It loses too. At least the phrase “one final bet” finally sounds ridiculous.

choices.label: Double down until you are even

outcomes.text: A lucky swing gets you back near even. Relief feels almost identical to panic.
The hole gets much deeper before you finally stop.

thread.title: The night I chased the loss
thread.memory: Trying to force the night back to even made chance feel personal.

title: A familiar dealer
text: The dealer recognizes you before you sit down and remembers a joke you made months ago.

choices.label: Chat, but keep the game casual

outcomes.text: The conversation makes the table feel human instead of hypnotic.
You talk more than you bet and leave almost exactly even.

choices.label: Ask whether luck has been good lately

outcomes.text: They laugh and remind you that the building did not get this big by losing.
They point at the ceiling cameras and say, “Luck has excellent management.”

choices.label: Take recognition as a sign to bet bigger

outcomes.text: The bigger bet lands. For one hand, confidence looks like prophecy.
Recognition was not the universe sending a signal. The larger bet disappears.

title: A friend wants a casino night
text: Someone close to you proposes a night at the casino and promises it is “just for fun.”

outcomes.text: You laugh more than you gamble and leave with the limit mostly intact.
The limit gets tested, but saying it out loud beforehand helps you stop.
You end up at dinner instead and nobody has to pretend a slot machine is conversation.
They tease you about being boring, then admit the food was better.
A silly scorecard turns tiny bets into a surprisingly fun rivalry.
Competition pushes both of you past the amount you meant to spend.

title: The number feels unreal
text: A large casino win hits your balance at once. For a few seconds, it looks more like a typo than money.

choices.label: Move most of it into real life

outcomes.text: Bills disappear, savings grow and the win becomes less exciting in exactly the right way.

thread.title: The win that changed the balance
thread.memory: A huge gambling win became real only after I decided what it was for.

outcomes.text: You save most of it and keep a small amount for fun. The split feels sane.
Dinner, shopping and a suite make one spectacular night.
The celebration expands to fit the win and then keeps expanding.

choices.label: Put it all back into action

outcomes.text: The next run is somehow even better. You leave before asking for a third miracle.
The casino gets a breathtaking amount of its money back.

title: Sails in the fog
text: A lookout spots another ship as a pale shadow through thick fog. Nobody can tell whether it is merchant, navy or another crew hunting the same water.

outcomes.text: It is a fat merchantman with sleepy watchmen. You take cargo before the fog lifts.

thread.title: The ship in the fog
thread.memory: We trusted a pale shape in bad visibility and found a prize instead of a patrol.

outcomes.text: The shadow resolves into navy colors much too late. You escape after a brutal chase.
Cannon reports in the distance tell you everything you needed to know. You let someone else have that trouble.
The fog clears on an empty horizon. Whatever it was is gone.
The other ship flees. Your crew cheers like that was the plan.
A cannon answers immediately. The fog becomes very exciting.

title: Three maps, one island
text: A fence in port lays out three treasure maps. All claim to show the same island. None agree on where the freshwater spring is.

outcomes.text: The parchment is ugly but accurate. A buried chest repays the gamble many times over.
The island is real; the treasure was found decades ago. You keep the map as a warning.
Fresh annotations lead you to a cave nobody else checked.
The “new” ink washes off in the rain. The seller is already gone.

choices.label: Compare all three and copy the overlaps

outcomes.text: The shared landmarks reveal a route none of the sellers understood.

thread.title: The three-map island
thread.memory: Three unreliable maps became useful only when I stopped trusting any single one.

outcomes.text: The overlaps lead to a swamp and several hours of inventive swearing.

title: Blood on the deck
text: A crew member takes a bad fall during rough weather. They are conscious, furious and clearly hurt.

choices.label: Put the ship into port for treatment

outcomes.text: The delay costs money, but the sailor returns to the ship on their own feet.
The port surgeon charges like royalty and does excellent work.
Careful splinting and a week off duty work better than anyone expected.
The sea is a poor hospital. Recovery is slow and morale dips.

choices.label: Tell them to shake it off

outcomes.text: They do, mostly out of spite, and never forget the order.
The injury worsens until you have no choice but to divert anyway.

title: The rival at the next table
text: Your rival captain is drinking in the same tavern, surrounded by enough crew to make violence a terrible idea and insults an irresistible one.

outcomes.text: The conversation is poisonous but useful. You learn where the patrols have been thickest.

thread.title: A drink with my rival
thread.memory: For one night, rivalry became intelligence gathering over a dirty table.

outcomes.text: They accept the drink and spend ten minutes explaining why your ship is ugly.
The tavern turns the insult into legend before either crew can draw steel.
A chair breaks, then another. You leave with a split lip and no clear winner.
Nothing annoys a rival like being denied the scene they rehearsed.
They loudly invent a story about why you are afraid. Half the tavern believes it.

title: Someone is in the hold
text: A barrel moves. Then it sneezes. A young stowaway crawls out from behind the cargo and says going back is not an option.

outcomes.text: You find a port where they have a cousin and enough coin for a new start.
They leave reluctantly, then wave from the dock until the ship is a dot.
They work hard, learn quickly and become part of the ship’s rhythm.

thread.title: The stowaway we kept
thread.memory: Someone entered the ship as hidden cargo and left the voyage as part of the crew.

outcomes.text: They are enthusiastic and catastrophically seasick, but the crew takes to them.
They hand over a hidden pouch of coins without complaint.
They have nothing. The demand turns the whole deck quiet.

title: The sea goes black
text: The pressure drops, birds disappear and the horizon takes on the color every sailor learns to respect.

choices.label: Reef sail early and ride it out

outcomes.text: The crew grumbles until the storm arrives. Then nobody questions the order.
Preparation saves the mast, but everyone works through a miserable night.
You beat the worst of the weather into shelter with minutes to spare.
The entrance is too dangerous and you are forced back into open water.

choices.label: Keep full sail and trust the ship

outcomes.text: For several terrifying hours, the ship flies faster than fear.
A line snaps and the deck becomes a battlefield of canvas and rope.

thread.title: The storm we challenged
thread.memory: We treated a black horizon like a dare and paid for the arrogance.

title: A navy cutter signals you to stop
text: A fast patrol vessel closes from windward and fires a shot across your bow.

outcomes.text: Your lighter draft wins. The cutter gives up before finding the reef the hard way.
You scrape the bottom escaping and spend the night listening to the hull creak.
For one miraculous minute, paperwork is stronger than cannon.
The patrol captain knows the flag code better than you hoped.
The officer discovers a sudden appreciation for administrative discretion.
They pocket the first payment and ask whether you would prefer jail or a second payment.

title: The crew counts the prize
text: A profitable voyage ends with everyone watching the quartermaster divide the take. The room is cheerful enough to become dangerous if the numbers feel wrong.

choices.label: Give the crew an extra share

outcomes.text: The cheer can be heard from the dock. Loyalty has a price and tonight you paid it willingly.
The extra share hurts your purse and buys a month without mutiny jokes.
Nobody can call it unfair. Nobody can call it generous either.
A few sailors mutter, but the rules were clear before the raid.
Nobody notices this time.
Someone notices the numbers do not add up. The joke about mutiny stops sounding like a joke.

thread.title: The share that did not add up
thread.memory: I learned how quickly a crew can smell dishonesty when money is on the table.

title: The air tastes metallic
text: A faint metallic taste spreads through the habitat. The oxygen numbers are technically normal, which somehow makes everyone more nervous.

choices.label: Seal sections and trace the source

outcomes.text: A damaged scrubber cartridge is isolated before readings turn dangerous.

thread.title: The metallic air
thread.memory: On Mars, a strange taste in the air once turned every breath into a systems question.

outcomes.text: The source is harder to find, but careful isolation keeps exposure low.
The taste fades and the numbers never move. Someone probably overheated a tool coating.
The sensor was calibrated wrong. The emergency alarm arrives late.

choices.label: Move everyone to the backup module

outcomes.text: The relocation is tedious and entirely worth the peace of mind.
The backup module is cramped enough to start three arguments before lunch.

title: Someone is stealing dessert
text: Inventory says twelve chocolate bars are missing. On Mars, this qualifies as both petty theft and a crisis of civilization.

outcomes.text: You find an honest counting error and save the colony from interrogating itself over candy.
The pattern points to one shift, but not one person. You tighten access without naming anyone.

choices.label: Make a joke of it at dinner

outcomes.text: The guilty colonist returns six bars anonymously by morning.
The joke lands badly with people already tired of rationing.

choices.label: Treat it as a serious security issue

outcomes.text: The theft stops immediately. So does casual conversation when you enter the pantry.
The investigation becomes more disruptive than the missing food ever was.

title: White fuzz in the greenhouse
text: A fast-growing fungus appears on one tray of crops. The agronomist says it may be harmless. “May” is doing a lot of work in that sentence.

outcomes.text: You lose vegetables and save the crop cycle.
The colony complains until a second tray shows spores and everyone stops complaining.
The fungus turns out to be benign and potentially useful for composting.
Containment fails and half the harvest has to be discarded.
The answer arrives late but useful: a low-tech heat treatment works.
The response arrives after the team has already solved it themselves.

title: The horizon disappears
text: A dust storm rolls over the colony until the windows show nothing but rust-colored static.

outcomes.text: The habitat goes quiet, dim and safe. The storm passes without major damage.
Conservation keeps life support stable through a longer storm than forecast.

choices.label: Use the storm to test exterior sensors

outcomes.text: The data is excellent and the equipment somehow survives.
One sensor tears loose and disappears into the red dark.
Mars looks enormous and hostile and beautiful enough to make everyone quiet.

thread.title: The storm that erased the horizon
thread.memory: A dust storm once made the whole world outside the glass disappear.

outcomes.text: A sudden impact against the dome ends the sightseeing instantly.

title: Seven minutes each way
text: You send an urgent technical question to Earth. The reply cannot arrive quickly enough for anyone there to make the decision for you.

outcomes.text: The fix works. For once, the communication delay feels like independence instead of isolation.
The fix is imperfect but stable enough to wait for expert review.
The answer is cautious, detailed and useful.
By the time the answer arrives, the situation has changed and half the advice is obsolete.

choices.label: Put it to the colony council

outcomes.text: The argument is loud and the decision belongs to everyone afterward.
Consensus takes so long that the original problem becomes two problems.

title: The rover did not come home
text: An autonomous rover misses its return window. Its last packet ended beside a shallow canyon thirty kilometers away.

outcomes.text: The rover is stuck on a rock that looks insultingly small once you arrive.
The trip becomes a cold, exhausting repair under a sky that offers no help.
A tiny steering correction frees it after six hours of patient commands.
The wheels spin deeper. Morning brings the same problem and less battery.
The colony hates losing equipment, but nobody risks a person for a machine.
A later satellite pass shows it sitting intact. The decision becomes a running joke.

title: Nobody agrees what the signal means
text: A repeating anomaly in the data has divided the habitat between “instrument noise,” “interesting,” and “please do not say aliens during breakfast.”

outcomes.text: A second instrument finds the same pattern. The room gets much quieter.

thread.title: The signal argument
thread.memory: Before anyone knew what it was, we argued about a repeating pattern in the static.

outcomes.text: The replication fails. Everyone learns something useful about wanting an answer too badly.

choices.label: Keep it confidential until there is proof

outcomes.text: The team works without outside pressure and documents every boring possibility first.
A rumor leaks anyway and Earth media invents an answer before the data does.
Researchers on Earth find a calibration artifact nobody on Mars considered.
The internet names the signal, merchandises it and starts arguments your team has no time for.

title: A birthday under another sky
text: The colony has become old enough that someone suggests celebrating its landing date like a birthday.

outcomes.text: Everyone gets one unnecessary meal, terrible decorations and an evening without work rotations.

thread.title: The colony birthday
thread.memory: We celebrated the day this place stopped being equipment and started becoming a home.

outcomes.text: The decorations keep falling in low gravity, which only makes people laugh harder.
A shared dessert and a speech are enough to change the mood for a night.
People appreciate the gesture, though someone loudly requests a real holiday next year.
A few veterans agree. Younger settlers roll their eyes with impressive coordination.
The shift proceeds normally and feels much longer than usual.

title: You are in the photograph
text: At a market stall, you find an old photograph of a crowd. Near the edge is a face that looks exactly like yours, wearing clothes from years before you arrived.

choices.label: Buy the photograph and hide it

outcomes.text: You tuck it into your private things and spend weeks comparing the background to places you know.

thread.title: The photograph that should not exist
thread.memory: I found my own face in a picture taken before I arrived.

outcomes.text: The seller mentions another copy exists somewhere. That information is not comforting.

choices.label: Ask the seller who the person is

outcomes.text: They shrug and give you a family name you have never heard.
They say the person was locally famous for disappearing without explanation.
You walk away and make it three blocks before turning back. The stall is gone.
You leave it. For years afterward, crowded photographs make you uneasy.

title: You know tomorrow’s headline
text: A public argument is raging over an event whose outcome you remember clearly from history.

outcomes.text: The event unfolds exactly as you remember. Keeping quiet feels safer and lonelier.
One small detail differs from your memory. You spend the night wondering why.

thread.title: The headline I remembered wrong
thread.memory: History once differed from my memory by one tiny detail, and I never learned why.

outcomes.text: The prediction comes true and someone begins treating you like a genius.
The prediction fails publicly enough to protect your secret by accident.

choices.label: Use the knowledge to make money

outcomes.text: A careful wager pays off without attracting much attention.
The opportunity has already moved differently than you remember. You lose money to your own certainty.

title: Medicine from another century
text: You are sick enough to need help, but the available medical advice belongs to a century you have read about for all the wrong reasons.

choices.label: Find the most cautious physician you can

outcomes.text: Clean instruments and restraint matter more than the doctor’s grand theories. You recover.
The treatment is uncomfortable but avoids the worst practices of the era.

choices.label: Use only knowledge you can safely explain

outcomes.text: Rest, clean water and basic hygiene do more than the dramatic remedies offered nearby.
Your advice attracts uncomfortable questions about where you learned it.
You get lucky and improve despite the treatment rather than because of it.
The remedy makes you significantly worse before your body turns the corner.

title: A voice from a wooden box
text: Radio ownership is spreading, and a family nearby invites everyone over to hear a broadcast as if the future has arrived in their sitting room.

choices.label: Enjoy it like it is new

outcomes.text: You let yourself be impressed by something you once took completely for granted.

thread.title: The first radio night
thread.memory: I heard a room experience broadcast audio as a miracle instead of background noise.

outcomes.text: The signal fades in and out, but nobody seems to mind.

choices.label: Explain where the technology will go

outcomes.text: Everyone thinks you are joking. That is probably for the best.
One technically minded guest starts asking questions you cannot safely answer.
Your indifference makes you look sophisticated instead of suspicious.
Someone asks what could possibly be more impressive. You have to invent an answer.

title: A room-sized future
text: A workplace has acquired a computer that occupies more space than some apartments. People argue about whether machines like it will ever matter outside institutions.

outcomes.text: You understand the concepts much faster than anyone expects and become the person everyone calls when it jams.
Knowing future interfaces does not make punch cards intuitive. You learn humility and the machine.

choices.label: Make a careful prediction about personal computers

outcomes.text: Everyone laughs at the idea of a computer in every home.
One colleague takes you seriously and starts sketching ideas that look uncomfortably familiar.

thread.title: The prediction someone believed
thread.memory: I mentioned a future technology too early and watched the idea take root in someone else.

outcomes.text: Avoiding the machine keeps your cover simple.
You miss an opportunity you know would have been historically interesting.

title: An idea not invented yet
text: A conversation turns toward a problem you know will eventually be solved by a very profitable invention.

outcomes.text: You change the subject and preserve one more piece of history from yourself.
Restraint feels noble until you remember what your bank balance looks like.
The inventor runs with the hint in a direction you did not expect.

thread.title: The idea I nudged
thread.memory: I gave history one small push and never learned whether it mattered.

outcomes.text: The explanation is too advanced for the available materials and dies as an interesting conversation.

choices.label: Try to claim the invention yourself

outcomes.text: You make money, but every success increases the fear of what else you changed.
Your prototype cannot be built reliably with current manufacturing. You lose money and credibility.

title: You used a word that does not exist yet
text: Conversation stops for half a beat after you use a piece of slang nobody around you recognizes.

choices.label: Pretend it is from your hometown

outcomes.text: People accept the explanation and immediately start using the word incorrectly.
Someone asks where your hometown is. The lie develops branches.
The moment disappears into conversation.
A friend keeps repeating the strange word because they like it.

thread.title: The word I brought too early
thread.memory: One careless piece of slang almost became evidence that I did not belong in the decade.

outcomes.text: Everyone assumes you are inventing nonsense for fun.
One person does not laugh and starts watching you much more carefully.

title: A familiar surname
text: Someone introduces themselves with a surname from your own family tree and mentions a hometown that makes the coincidence much harder to dismiss.

outcomes.text: You learn almost nothing and preserve the safest possible distance.
A harmless family detail confirms the connection anyway.

choices.label: Ask careful questions about their family

outcomes.text: You hear a story that survived into your childhood in a completely different form.

thread.title: A family story before it became history
thread.memory: I met someone connected to my family before the story reached my generation.

outcomes.text: The questions become too specific and they ask why you care so much.
You choose ignorance on purpose. It feels strangely responsible.
You leave quickly enough to look suspicious and spend the day checking who followed you.

title: The rival remembers
text: Years later, your rival captain repeats a detail from that old tavern encounter that you assumed nobody important noticed.

choices.label: Use the shared history to bargain

outcomes.text: Old hostility becomes a temporary truce over a profitable route.
The bargain works, but neither crew stops watching the other.

choices.label: Remind them you are still rivals

outcomes.text: The argument becomes performance. Both crews cheer and nobody draws steel.
The old insult lands harder than intended and the truce evaporates.
Their version is different enough to make you question your own memory.
They remember the exact moment you were hoping they forgot.

title: A debt from the hold
text: The former stowaway finds you again, older and carrying news from a port you thought had forgotten your name.

outcomes.text: Their warning about an ambush saves the ship a week later.
The news is mostly gossip, but seeing them alive and capable is reward enough.
They rejoin for one voyage and work like someone with something to prove.
They smile and refuse. They built a life on land and wanted you to know.
You exchange a nod and let the past remain a complete story.
They leave hurt that you remembered the problem better than the person.

title: The missing coins return
text: The old dispute over a crew share resurfaces when the quartermaster finds a ledger page that never matched the official count.

outcomes.text: The confession costs coin and pride, but the crew respects finally hearing the truth.
The crew takes the repayment without forgiving the lie.
Enough people accept the explanation to end the meeting.
The quartermaster produces a second page in your handwriting.
Coin is distributed and nobody asks why you suddenly became generous.
The unexplained generosity convinces half the crew you stole even more than they suspected.

title: What the rover saw
text: Data recovered from the rover includes a geological pattern nobody noticed during the rescue.

outcomes.text: The formation contains useful ice deposits close enough to change planning.
The pattern is geologically interesting but not economically useful.
Researchers pick up the result and credit the colony team properly.
Earth researchers argue over the interpretation for months.
A later planning team is grateful you kept the raw files organized.
The data sits untouched, another quiet possibility under a very large sky.

title: The pattern returns
text: The anomaly that divided the habitat appears again on a different instrument, during a different shift, with the same strange spacing.

choices.label: Treat it as a real research program

outcomes.text: The colony dedicates scheduled time to replication instead of arguing in hallways.
Formal study makes the anomaly less exciting and much more credible.

choices.label: Send the full record to Earth

outcomes.text: Independent observatories confirm that something unusual is there.
Earth finds no match, which is somehow more unsettling than a mundane explanation.
The small team works carefully without spectacle.
Secrecy breeds rumors faster than data can answer them.

title: A familiar invention
text: Years after your careful hint, a newspaper describes a new product whose central idea sounds uncomfortably close to that old conversation.

choices.label: Accept that history may have absorbed the nudge

outcomes.text: The world keeps moving and nobody points at you. You decide that is enough.
A tiny design detail matches your exact wording. The coincidence is difficult to dismiss.
They barely remember the conversation and insist the solution came from years of work.
They recognize you immediately and ask how you knew.
You add another page to a notebook nobody else can ever safely read.
The notebook already contains a version of the event that did not happen this way.

title: A family object before it was an heirloom
text: The person tied to your family history shows you an ordinary household object you recognize from stories told generations later.

outcomes.text: The real origin is smaller, stranger and more human than the family legend.
The story contradicts what your family always believed, and now only you know.
You let the object remain ordinary in its own time.
The silence feels like protecting a memory that technically has not happened yet.

choices.label: Leave a tiny mark where your family will one day find it

outcomes.text: The mark is subtle enough to become a mystery instead of proof.
You stop yourself halfway through, frightened by how badly you want evidence.

title: The second copy
text: In another city, another shop has the same impossible photograph—except one person in the background is missing from this copy.

outcomes.text: Everything else matches. The missing figure is the only difference.
A second difference appears after an hour: a storefront sign uses a name you do not remember.
The evidence is gone. The memory is not.
You burn it and immediately wonder whether the other copy changed.

choices.label: Hide both copies in separate places

outcomes.text: You create a private test for whether the timeline changes again.
One hiding place is empty when you return months later.

title: The win after the excitement
text: Years later, the casino win is no longer a flashing number. It is whatever you turned it into—or whatever is left.

choices.label: Look at what the money changed

outcomes.text: Savings, purchases and paid-off obligations tell a quieter story than the original jackpot did.
The balance is smaller than you remember, but several problems are gone because of it.

choices.label: Go back to the casino for nostalgia

outcomes.text: You play small, enjoy the memory and leave without trying to recreate it.
The old feeling returns faster than expected and you leave uneasy.
The win has become one strange chapter among many.
A promotional email still knows exactly which memory to press on.

title: The buyer comes back
text: The person who once made an unsolicited offer returns with a new number and a note saying they are still serious.

outcomes.text: The number is higher enough to make the room go quiet.
The new offer is barely different. You decline without drama.

choices.label: Ask why they want this house

outcomes.text: Their reason is personal: a relative once lived nearby and they have been trying to return for years.
They give a vague investment answer that makes the whole thing feel less mysterious.

choices.label: Tell them the house is not for sale

outcomes.text: They finally accept the answer. The house feels oddly more yours afterward.
They leave a business card anyway. You throw it in a drawer.

title: The holiday became tradition
text: Years after the first landing-day celebration, children in the habitat argue over the “correct” way to decorate for it.

outcomes.text: They invent traditions nobody from the landing crew would have imagined.
Their version is louder and sillier than yours. That is probably a good sign.
The old meal and speech still mean something, especially to the veterans.
The younger colonists participate politely and immediately add their own traditions afterward.
The celebration gains weight without losing joy.
A few stories are too heavy for a party, but nobody asks you to stop.
